page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v6 is an Eav6-family memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64as_v6 demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and image processing, placing in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core and image processing metrics. It also achieves top-tier throughput for prompt processing with small language models. Memory performance is strong, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4863.52 GB/sec and large-block write bandwidth at 108.95 GB/sec, both in the top 25%. However, uncached large-block read bandwidth is average at 154.03 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded decompression and database operations remain strong.

The instance offers high memory density and strong multi-core compute capabilities, making it a resource-dense option for memory-intensive workloads. A key tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on external network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads depending on the attached storage tier. Given its 512.0 GB memory capacity and strong multi-core performance, the E64as_v6 is suited for large database deployments, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
